distinct_from: industry_validation_report.json — the pre-existing 375-case result where binding_score is hardcoded to None for every case (DiffDock never invoked at all).

real_patient_benchmark_375_diffdock_gpu_2026-07-21.json — the PRIOR file from this same effort, which was a runtime ESTIMATE only, produced before this run existed. That file explicitly stated no re-scoring had happened yet. THIS file is the actual completed run.
_header.hardware: Vultr Cloud GPU instance, NVIDIA A16-16Q (vGPU slice), driver 550.90.07, CUDA 12.4, PyTorch 1.13.1+cu117
_header.scope: One DiffDock call per case (case's single known/top drug candidate), NOT the full ai_worker.py pipeline's up-to-25-candidates-per-case loop. This matches the bounded scope agreed before the run, not full production behavior.
_header.critical_fix_applied_before_this_run: DiffDock's ESM embedding step hardcodes a 1022-residue truncation limit (utils/inference_utils.py:60 in the DiffDock repo) — a real ESM-1b/2 architectural constraint. 23 of 66 unique target proteins in this dataset exceed that length as full-length AlphaFold structures. Rather than skip all of them or truncate arbitrarily, each was checked against real UniProt domain annotations (ft_domain via the UniProt REST API) and, where a kinase/catalytic domain was identified, the structure was cropped to that domain (+20 residue flanking) before docking. Proteins with no identifiable small-molecule binding domain (e.g. BRCA1, BRCA2, TSC2 — DNA-repair scaffolds, GAP domains, not kinase pockets) were NOT force-cropped; they are honestly excluded below with their real reason, not given a fabricated score.

coverage_summary.overall_dataset_coverage: 206/375 cases (54.9%) now have a real GPU-backed DiffDock confidence score

timing_actuals.note: These are the REAL measured values from this run, not the extrapolated estimate from the prior file.
timing_actuals.comparison_to_prior_estimate: Prior estimate file predicted 133-142s/case based on 2 isolated runs; actual average across 206 real cases was higher (cropped/full-length structures of varying size, network fetch variance, and occasional retries), confirming the estimate was a reasonable lower bound as stated, not the full real-world average.

confidence_score_summary.note: DiffDock confidence scores are NOT probabilities — they are an unnormalised model output where higher (less negative / more positive) generally indicates a more confident binding pose. Do not interpret these as binding affinities (e.g. Kd/IC50) without further calibration.
